pages.text: $(italic)$(#6b5a45)Put the file in your datapack under $(#8a5a2b)data/<namespace>/craft_recipes/$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) and reopen the$(br) Crafting Station after $(#8a5a2b)/reload$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45). $(bold)The file name is the recipe id$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45);$(br) the $(#8a5a2b)id$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) field inside is read by nothing, so renaming the file renames the recipe.$()
Every row in the Crafting Station's wand and gadget list, and every row in the Magic Workshop's scroll list, is backed by a $(#8a5a2b

)craft_recipes$() file. These recipes do not use the vanilla $(#8a5a2b)pattern$()/$(#8a5a2b)key$() shape: they state only how many el$(br)ements something costs and what it produces, and a mage does the work in town.

The ordinary datapack path, $(#8a5a2b)data/<namespace>/craft_recipes/<id>.json$(), takes effect on $(#8a5a2b)/reload$().$(br2)To override a recipe the mod ships, your file $(bold)must sit in the $(#8a5a2b)wandscape$()$(bold) namespace under the same file name
pages.title: Where the Files Go

pages.text: $(): the registry key is the file name with the namespace stripped away, and when two namespaces collide the mod's own copy wins whil$(br)e the other is dropped in silence.

$(bold)Key  Meaning$()$(li)type — $(#8a5a2b)wand$(), $(#8a5a2b)spell$(), $(#8a5a2b)misc$() or $(#8a5a2b)potion$(); absent means $(#8a5a2b)wand$()$(li)output — the product, which must carry at least $(#8a5a2b)item$()$(li)cost — a map from element to a whole number
pages.title: Fields Every Recipe Shares

pages.text: unlock_requirement — only $(#8a5a2b)min_colony_level$() is read, default 1$(li)craft_station — labels the station on the JEI page only$(li)display_name — $(bold)read by no code at all$()

Get $(#8a5a2b)type$() wrong by a single letter and the file is $(bold)dropped in silence$() — no error, no warning. An element key th$(br)at does not exist makes the whole file fail to parse, which at least leaves a warning in the log.
pages.title: What a Typo Costs

pages.text: A recipe row shows neither $(#8a5a2b)display_name$() nor the file name, but the language key $(#8a5a2b)craft_recipe.wandscape.<recipe$(br) id>$(), falling back to $(bold)the product item's own name$(). A wand recipe with no language key therefore shows up as plain "Wand"$(br) next to every other un-named wand.
pages.title: The Name on the Screen

pages.text: Language files live on the $(#8a5a2b)assets$() side, so $(bold)a pure datapack cannot supply one$(). To choose the name yourself the $(br)pack has to ship $(#8a5a2b)assets/<namespace>/lang/en_us.json$() alongside its data and fill in that key.
pages.title: Where Language Files Live

pages.text: $(bold)Wands$()$(br2)$(#8a5a2b)output.item$() must be $(#8a5a2b)wandscape:wand$(), $(#8a5a2b)wand_color$() takes a $(#8a5a2b)#RRGGBB$() string, and the mo$(br)difiers go in the $(#8a5a2b)attributes$() array, each entry carrying three keys: $(#8a5a2b)type$(), $(#8a5a2b)operation$() and $(#8a5a2b)amount$().

$(#8a5a2b)type$() is one of nine: $(#8a5a2b)max_hp$(), $(#8a5a2b)move_speed$(), $(#8a5a2b)spell_power$(), $(#8a5a2b)work_speed$(), $(#8a5a2b)spell_speed$(), $(#8a5a2b)armor_value$(), $(#8a5a2b)max_mana$(), $(#8a5a2b)health_regen$(), $(#8a5a2b)mana_regen$().$(br2)$(bold)What a Wand Is$()$(br2)A wand has no tier or class field: what a wand $(italic)is$() is exactly this set of modifiers plus a colour.
pages.title: Writing the Modifiers

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)operation$() is either $(#8a5a2b)addition$(), which adds the amount outright, or $(#8a5a2b)multiply_base$(), which adds a p$(br)ercentage of the base value. $(#8a5a2b)amount$() is therefore sometimes $(#8a5a2b)40.0$() and sometimes $(#8a5a2b)0.2$(), and negative numbers are legal.
The modifiers $(bold)apply to a mage holding the wand and to nobody else$() — a player holding one gets nothing. And a misspelled enu
pages.title: Two Things That Bite

pages.text: m value inside $(#8a5a2b)attributes$() costs you the preset variant in the creative inventory while $(bold)the recipe itself still cr$(br)afts$(), so the result is a wand that$(br2)exists, crafts fine, and carries no modifiers at all.

Set $(#8a5a2b)type$() to $(#8a5a2b)spell$(), use $(#8a5a2b)wandscape:spell_scroll$() for $(#8a5a2b)output.item$(), and point $(#8a5a2$(br)b)output.magic_id$() at the magic to bind. The default $(#8a5a2b)craft_station$() is $(#8a5a2b)magic_station$().
pages.title: Scrolls

pages.text: Omit $(#8a5a2b)output.magic_id$() and it $(bold)defaults to the recipe's own file name$() rather than to any magic id. A recipe calle$(br)d $(#8a5a2b)scroll_heal.json$() that leaves it out binds to a magic named $(#8a5a2b)scroll_heal$(), which very likely does not exist.
pages.title: What magic_id Defaults To

pages.text: Nothing validates it at load time, an$(br2)d the price of the typo is a scroll that does nothing when used and reports unknown data.

Set $(#8a5a2b)type$() to $(#8a5a2b)misc$() and put any item id in $(#8a5a2b)output.item$(). One item comes out per craft and the play$(br)er picks the quantity in the screen. This type has no $(#8a5a2b)count$() or $(#8a5a2b)nbt$() field to write.
pages.title: Gadgets

pages.text: A $(#8a5a2b)potion$() type also exists, supporting a product with NBT and extra ingredients; the mod itself does not use it anywhere.

What you write into $(#8a5a2b)cost$() is a $(bold)unit price$(). The amount actually paid is multiplied by the server's element craft$(br)-cost multiplier (1.0 by default, adjustable in the Settings Center) and rounded up, and a player raising the output quantity scales
pages.title: Costs Get Multiplied

pages.text: the cost linearly with it. Keep that l$(br2)ayer in mind when tuning: a thousand in the JSON is not a thousand out of the player's warehouse.
